PullRequest.Title: Engineering - install every pnpm root with the isolated linker
PullRequest.Body:

This is part of the pnpm migration. It switches every pnpm install root from `nodeLinker: hoisted` to `isolated`, with one commit per root: the main workspace, `remote`, `extensions`, `extensions/copilot`, `build` and `test/sanity`. No lockfile changes. It builds on #346923 (packaging that works with either linker), #346940, #346907, #346965 and #347205 (Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions cache the pnpm store instead of `node_modules`, so the layout of `node_modules` no longer matters for the caches).

It's a draft, to run the CI and product builds in Azure Pipelines before review. It has only been validated locally on macOS arm64 so far (see below).

## Changes

- **Main workspace:** the linker switch. The pre-check of the Codex smoke test looked for `@openai/codex-<platform>` only in the root `node_modules`. It now also looks next to the real folder of `@openai/codex`.
- **`remote`:** the linker switch, and the comments about `remote/web` in `build/npm/dirs.ts` and `build/gulpfile.vscode.web.ts`.
- **`extensions`:** the linker switch, and the comment on `hoistWorkspacePackages`.
- **`extensions/copilot`:**
  - `vsce package` lists the production dependencies with `npm list`, which can't read the symlinked `node_modules` of the isolated layout. The `package` script now runs `script/build/packageVsix.ts`, which runs `vsce package` in a staging folder that `pnpm deploy --prod` creates. The Copilot pipeline calls the script.
  - `debug` tries to load `supports-color`, an optional peer that isn't installed. esbuild bundled whichever copy it could reach, which depends on the layout, so it's now external in the extension host bundle.
  - When chat-lib is extracted, TypeScript can't name TypeBox's types in the declarations of the schemas through the symlinks (TS2883). The files that define the schemas now export those types.
- **`build`** and **`test/sanity`:** the linker switch only. The sanity jobs cache the pnpm store, and the containers that bind-mount `test/sanity` can use the layout, because pnpm's links are relative.
- **Copilot CI jobs:** Copilot's lint uses the root ESLint configuration, which loads the local rules in `.eslint-plugin-local`. The Copilot jobs installed only the root project (`--filter .`), and the lint found the rules' dependencies, such as `@typescript-eslint/utils`, through the root's hoisting. The Azure Pipelines Copilot setup and the GitHub Copilot jobs, which share their pnpm store caches, now also install `.eslint-plugin-local` (`--filter vscode-eslint-plugin-local`).
- **Windows test jobs on GitHub Actions:** esbuild follows pnpm's junctions with Go's `os.Readlink`, which by default for esbuild turns the volume behind a mount point into a drive letter path. These jobs mount their Dev Drive or workspace image at the parent of the workspace without a drive letter, so esbuild couldn't resolve the dependencies of packages ("Could not resolve `@hpke/common`"). `pr-win32-test.yml` now sets `GODEBUG=winreadlinkvolume=1`, so that `Readlink` keeps the volume path. Some paths in esbuild's source maps may then be absolute in these jobs.

Existing checkouts switch layout on the next `pnpm install`, with no manual step.

## What changes in the output

The packages contain the same files as with the hoisted linker, apart from renamed webview chunks. Besides rebuilt native modules, these files differ:
- The Copilot `extension.js` no longer bundles `supports-color`, or the second copies of `semver` and `content-type` that the hoisted layout installed in two folders. It also no longer bundles the optional `bufferutil`, `utf-8-validate` and `node-gyp-build` of `ws`, which it reached through the root's hoisting; `ws` falls back to JavaScript either way.
- The HTML language server and the TypeScript web server no longer bundle a second copy of `vscode-languageserver-textdocument` and `vscode-uri`.
- The chunk names of the Markdown and Mermaid webviews change, because their content includes the module paths.
- Some source maps list different `sources` paths.

The esbuild inputs of all 82 built-in extension builds have the same packages and versions, and the Copilot builds differ only as described above. The Copilot VSIX has the same 82 files as `vsce package` run directly on the same build.

## Known issues

- **OSS license scan:** `build/azure-pipelines/oss/scan-licenses.ts` keys packages by name, so for a package installed in several versions it reports a different version than with the hoisted layout (same package names). It should key by name and version.
- **Not yet validated:** Windows (long `.pnpm` paths, native builds, `zx.cmd` in signing), Linux and Alpine containers, and the product pipeline.

## Validation

All on macOS arm64, with offline installs from the local pnpm store:

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`: passed for every root, lockfiles unchanged. Switching an existing install in place works in both directions.
- `pnpm exec npm-run-all2 -lp --continue-on-error eslint stylelint hygiene core-ci-pr valid-layers-check 'gulp compile-extensions'`: passed.
- `cd build && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test`: 1493 passed, 1 failed (`next/test/resources.test.ts`: `/var` vs `/private/var` on macOS, which also fails with hoisted).
- `cd extensions/copilot && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run compile && pnpm run package`: passed.
- The Copilot jobs' installs in a clean checkout: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --filter .`, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in `extensions/copilot`, then `pnpm run lint` there failed with the CI's `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `@typescript-eslint/utils`. With `--filter . --filter vscode-eslint-plugin-local`, the lint passed (2285 files).
- `test/sanity`: `pnpm run compile`, loading every test module (`node out/index.js` with a `--grep` that matches no test), `pnpm run test-copilot-shim-helper` and `pnpm run test-copilot-shim-rendering`: passed, also from a copy in another folder. The local store doesn't have `yargs@17.7.3`, so this used 17.7.2 (not committed).

Before rebasing onto `main` (the same commits; `main` didn't change the packaging code since), with the same results as the hoisted linker, apart from local environment failures that also occur with it:
- `pnpm run gulp --series --continue vscode-darwin-arm64-min vscode-reh-darwin-arm64-min vscode-reh-web-darwin-arm64-min vscode-web-min`, compared with hoisted after each root's switch: the differences listed above. Locally the `-min` builds of desktop and server stop at `prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim` with either linker.
- Unit tests in Node.js, Electron and WebKit.
- Integration tests: Electron (`./scripts/test-integration.sh`, also `--suite copilot`), web and remote.
- Smoke tests: `pnpm run smoketest-no-compile`, also with `--web` and `--remote`.
- Copilot: `pnpm run lint`, the unit, prompt and simulation tests, and the chat-lib job.
- The OSS license scan: the differences described above.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after subprocess sequence, manifest dependency closure, lack of a `files` bound, ignore-file allowlist, and synchronous cleanup are all directly visible. Exact elapsed time depends on filesystem/link behavior and cache warmth, which affects severity but not the I/O amplification mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem operations and bytes for a full temporary project plus hoisted production dependency tree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each packaging invocation copies work proportional to the entire extensions/copilot source tree and all transitive production dependencies, then recursively deletes that staging tree; the final VSIX remains constrained by .vscodeignore to a small allowlist.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased Copilot VSIX packaging latency and temporary disk usage on local and product-build critical paths
Findings.PreviousBehavior: `vsce package` ran directly in extensions/copilot and traversed the installed dependency graph without first creating and deleting another complete deployment.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added synchronous `pnpm deploy --prod` creates a hoisted portable copy of the project and every production dependency before `vsce` packages it, after which the entire staging directory is synchronously removed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 30 adds the full `pnpm deploy --prod --config.node-linker=hoisted` subprocess before the existing packager; this deployment and its later recursive deletion did not exist in the previous direct `vsce package` path.
Findings.Title: Limit staging to files that can enter the VSIX
Findings.Impact: Every `pnpm run package`, including the Product Copilot pipeline, now waits for an additional full-tree deployment and cleanup. This scales with the large Copilot source tree and its 40+ direct production dependencies even though `.vscodeignore` starts with `**` and admits only the built artifacts and selected dependency files.
Findings.Evidence: Added line 30 invokes `pnpm deploy --prod` into a fresh temp directory; lines 44-45 then run the pre-existing `vsce package`, and line 42 recursively removes the deployment. `extensions/copilot/package.json` has no `files` allowlist and declares 40+ production dependencies, while `.vscodeignore` excludes everything by default and selectively includes only build outputs, the server plugin, and selected `@github/copilot` files. The changed product pipeline calls this script on its packaging critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the flat dependency layout needed by `vsce`, but construct the staging deployment from a package/files allowlist matching the VSIX inputs (or otherwise stage only the built artifacts and explicitly included dependency/plugin files) so source, tests, and excluded production packages are never copied and deleted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install dependencies in the main, remote, extensions, Copilot, build, and sanity pnpm roots
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `pnpm install` must finish before compilation, lint, tests, and product builds. The linker change affects filesystem layout during that existing critical-path install but does not add a package set or a new install invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: pnpm-workspace.yaml and the five nested pnpm-workspace.yaml files, `nodeLinker`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Import/link dependency files from the pnpm store and create the isolated node_modules symlink graph
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install layout operation per package graph entry in each invoked root, with the same package graph as before
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same installs imported the same locked packages into a hoisted node_modules layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before dependent build/test commands can start

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Existing `pnpm install` invocations across setup workflows/scripts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch package tarballs on pnpm-store misses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only missing packages in the unchanged lockfile graph; zero on a fully warm store
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold installs fetched the same locked packages; warm installs used the same pnpm-store cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold-cache misses block install completion; warm-cache builds avoid them

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The existing lockfile package graph in each of six install roots; the PR states no lockfile changes, so effective package cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: pnpm performs its normal internal fetch/import/link concurrency within each root; separate CI jobs can install independently. The diff adds no shared burst, limiter change, or serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm pnpm-store installs reuse package contents but relink node_modules; cold installs fetch the same locked package graph as before. Existing workflow store caches remain the cache boundary and are not invalidated by node_modules layout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that only dependency layout changes here; no concrete performance regression is established from the configuration switch alone.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact link/import operation counts and filesystem performance vary by platform, especially Windows junction handling, but there is no evidence that the isolated layout adds package downloads or unbounded work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff changes layout without changing package cardinality, network fan-out, cache keys, or install concurrency, and no measured or code-proven slowdown is present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prepare dependencies for Copilot lint jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The root install must complete before Copilot lint loads the repository ESLint configuration and local rules.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run pnpm install with the added `vscode-eslint-plugin-local` filter
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install invocation per affected Copilot CI job; the diff expands the selected graph rather than adding another subprocess
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same install selected only the root project and omitted the local ESLint rule workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks lint/test setup, as did the prior root install

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .eslint-plugin-local/package.json dependency graph reached by the changed filters
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch dependencies unique to the local ESLint workspace on store misses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the plugin's bounded dependency closure per cold shared store, reduced by overlap with root dependencies
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Those packages were not selected solely for this workspace, although overlapping root packages could already be present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only cold-store misses extend setup; warm shared stores avoid fetches

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional local workspace package with nine declared dev dependencies per affected install definition; effective fetched cardinality is only dependencies absent from the root graph/store.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pnpm install subprocess per CI job; six changed job/setup definitions may execute in separate CI jobs, while each invocation is handled by pnpm's existing internal concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pnpm-store workflows skip installs on a matching saved store, and other jobs reuse the store. On cold misses, only previously absent plugin dependencies require network fetch; workspace linking still occurs when install runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the bounded graph expansion, but low confidence in meaningful performance impact because the dependencies are required for lint correctness, heavily overlap tooling already installed, and are cached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact incremental package count depends on graph overlap and store warmth.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this is bounded, necessary setup work within an existing install and no actionable avoidable fan-out or concurrency amplification is shown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Package the Copilot extension locally or in the Product Copilot pipeline
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new `pnpm deploy` completes synchronously before `vsce package`; packaging then completes before artifact publication. Temporary-tree deletion also runs synchronously before the script exits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a hoisted production deployment in a fresh temporary directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full deployment per package invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No deployment subprocess or temporary production tree was created; vsce packaged directly from extensions/copilot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New blocking stage before the existing packager

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy/materialize the project and production dependency closure, copy the server plugin, then recursively delete the staging tree
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Filesystem work proportional to the complete staged project and transitive production graph per invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: vsce read package inputs in place and did not create/delete a second complete deployment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All materialization and cleanup block script completion and product artifact publication

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `vsce package` against the staging folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The product pipeline invoked the same packager directly in the Copilot source directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing packaging critical path, now sequenced after deploy

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The complete Copilot project file tree plus its 40+ direct and transitive production dependencies, despite the final VSIX being restricted by `.vscodeignore` to built artifacts and selected dependency/plugin files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The deploy, manifest/plugin copies, vsce subprocess, and recursive cleanup are strictly serialized through `spawnSync` and synchronous filesystem APIs; there is no coalescing across invocations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm pnpm store can avoid downloads, but every invocation creates a fresh temp directory and still materializes and deletes the deployment. There is no reusable staging cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the new deploy, strict sequencing, broad dependency manifest, restrictive VSIX ignore file, and recursive cleanup are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Elapsed time depends on filesystem/link strategy, platform, and dependency sizes; the extra full-tree materialization remains certain even on a warm store.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: avoidable eager filesystem work now scales with the whole project/dependency closure rather than the small final VSIX input set.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build and activate the Copilot Node extension bundle
Scenarios.CriticalPath: esbuild treats `supports-color` as external during compilation. At extension activation, `debug` performs its normal optional module resolution once when its module initializes; activation does not wait on a new network or subprocess boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the external optional `supports-color` module at runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached optional resolution per module instance/process
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reachable `supports-color` copy was bundled, so its code loaded from the extension bundle rather than external module resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A small fixed module-initialization lookup during extension loading

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One optional module resolution per loaded `debug` module instance, not per log event, request, editor, or message.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous Node module resolution during module initialization; fixed cardinality with no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node's module cache coalesces subsequent requires within the extension host process. The optional module is absent in this install layout, so the first lookup falls back to `debug` basic colors.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-time changed resolution behavior and high confidence that it lacks realistic scaling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact filesystem stat count depends on Node resolution paths, but cardinality is fixed and tiny.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this replaces bundled optional code with one cached lookup and does not create a meaningful hot/scaling performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the Agents Window Codex smoke-test precheck and Windows esbuild jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The development smoke test performs its synchronous binary precheck once before spawning Codex tests. Windows builds use the changed Go readlink behavior while esbuild resolves package junctions; those resolutions remain part of the existing build path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the real path of `@openai/codex`, inspect one or two vendor directories, and test candidate binaries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One precheck over one deduplicated location in flat installs or two locations in isolated development installs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inspected one flat platform-package vendor directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only this smoke-test setup and remains fixed/small

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve pnpm junction targets through Go `os.Readlink` during esbuild jobs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing set of package junction resolutions performed by esbuild
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same readlink calls occurred but could return drive-letter paths for mounted volumes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on the existing Windows build/test path; the setting preserves volume paths so resolution succeeds

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most two Codex scope locations and the small set of vendor triples for the smoke precheck; existing module/junction count for each esbuild job.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The smoke checks are sequential synchronous filesystem calls once per test setup. Esbuild retains its existing build concurrency; the environment variable changes path representation, not concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit application cache for the smoke precheck, but it runs once. OS filesystem caches may warm repeated esbuild path resolution; no cache key or lifecycle changes are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the extra smoke-test filesystem work is bounded and test-only and that GODEBUG changes semantics rather than call count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Vendor triple count and esbuild module graph vary, but neither changed path creates unbounded or collection-wide duplicate work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: added smoke-test I/O is one bounded preflight check, while the Windows setting does not increase boundary cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 20 changed files and their relevant callers. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence finding for full-tree Copilot VSIX staging I/O; no other changed path established an actionable scaling or critical-path performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
